replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Unauthenticated shared queue plus card-charging payments agent supports concrete spoofing-to-charge attack."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Evidence shows multiple agents on same unauthenticated queue; least-privilege violation distinct from spoofing by external actor."},{"id":"T3","keep":true,"reason":"Planner delegates to flights agent and payments agent; injected tool output hijacking payments is concrete."},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Lack of sender authentication on queue directly supports non-attributability of charge instructions."},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"Unauthenticated queue carrying payment/trip data supports concrete disclosure to any queue-accessing process."},{"id":"T6","keep":true,"reason":"Unauthenticated messages permit in-transit modification of amount/token; tampering distinct from spoofed-sender injection."}]}
